Baseline 'running_mean' with window 2 expects the mean of the previous two raw values, this one excluded, so the history is [], [1], [1,-2], [-2,0.5], [0.5,0] and expected is 0, 1, -0.5, -0.75, 0.25; delta is therefore 1, -3, 1, 0.75, 2.75; relu applied [1], [0], [1], [0.75], [2.75] with clearance boost 0, 3, 0, 0, 0; split applied [1,0], [0,3], [1,0], [0.75,0], [2.75,0] with clearance boost 0 throughout. The four values stay apart in every record: Raw is the argument unchanged, Expected is the baseline, Transformed is Raw - Expected with its sign, Applied is the non-negative per-channel release and ClearanceBoost is the non-negative clearance term that the relu kind produces instead of a negative release. Negative feedback never becomes a negative release: over the sequence [-5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 5, -1] on all four combinations every applied value and every clearance boost was finite, at or above zero and not a negative zero, and relu always produced one channel while split always produced two. The record belongs to the caller: after keeping the first record and mapping -4 and 7, the first record's Applied, Raw, Expected and Transformed were unchanged, and writing 99 into that record did not move the baseline, which was still the mean of -4 and 7, that is 1.5. A non-finite raw value is refused and does not enter the history: after NaN, +Inf and -Inf were each refused, the next expected value was still 2, the mean of the one accepted value. Seven invalid declarations are refused: an unknown baseline, no baseline, an unknown kind, no kind, a window declared with baseline 'none' (a knob that would never be read), baseline 'running_mean' without a window and a negative window. The race detector reports nothing.
assumption_statement: The baseline and the mapping kind are declarations, not learned quantities: 'none' expects zero and 'running_mean' expects the arithmetic mean of the previous Window raw values with equal weight, and with fewer than Window values it is the mean of the values there are, the first value having no history and expecting zero. That convention is a choice; another reasonable convention would refuse to map until the window is full. Requiring Window to be zero for baseline 'none' is also a choice, made so that no declaration can carry a knob that is silently ignored. The clearance boost of the relu kind is recorded as a non-negative number only; what it does to a concentration is ticket 21.
